deep.reconstruction:
Page 9 of the 1983 notes. It continues the programme from p. 8: one homotopy theory H, as a 2-functor A -> H(A) on small categories, is presented by various pairs (M,W). The page tests this on a second example, then lists 'formal properties', in effect axioms, that such an H(A) should satisfy.

Ex 4. Take M = complexes in an abelian category 𝒜 and W = quasi-isomorphisms.
- Hom(A,M) is the category of complexes in the functor category Hom(A,𝒜).
- W_A is the class of objectwise quasi-isomorphisms.
- H(A) = D(Hom(A,𝒜)), the derived category of A-diagrams.

When 𝒜 = sheaves of k-modules on a topos T, Hom(A,𝒜) is the category of sheaves of k-modules on the product topos (A^o)^∧ ×_top T, where (A^o)^∧ is the presheaf topos of A^o. For f: A -> B, restriction f^* is the inverse image along the topos morphism f^o_top × id_T. f^* is exact, so it passes to derived categories directly; there it has a right adjoint Rf_* (derived right Kan extension, i.e. homotopy limits over comma categories).

On the left adjoint, G. first writes that there is 'generally no left adjoint, presumably', marking an exception or question for T = point, 𝒜 = k-modules. He then observes that the left adjoint (f^o_top)_! (left Kan extension) always exists at sheaf level. If it is also left exact, it is exact on complexes, preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and so descends to Lf_!.

Formal properties.
- Hyp 4 (base change). For a cartesian square A' -> A over B' -> B:
  - g^* f_! <- f'_! g'^* is an isomorphism if f is cofibrant, i.e. a Grothendieck opfibration ('catégorie cofibrée'), 'or g fibrant ??'.
  - g^* f_* ≅ f'_* g'^* if f is fibrant (a Grothendieck fibration), 'or g cofibrant ??'.
  - He notes the second family follows from the first by passing to right adjoints.
- Hyp 5. If f is fully faithful, then f^*_H is a (Bousfield-type) localization: f_! and f_* are fully faithful, i.e. f^* f_! ≅ id ≅ f^* f_*.
- Hyp 6. If f: A -> B is a localization of categories, then f^*_H is fully faithful, f_! and f_* are localizations, and f_! f^* ≅ f_* f^* ≅ id.

Purpose: these are the axioms of a 'théorie homotopique' (a precursor of the derivator axioms Der 1–4 of Les Dérivateurs, 1990–91). Derived categories of diagrams serve as a model case. The next page continues with cofinality and with ∫_A = p_!.
errors: Over-pessimism about the derived left adjoint. Derived left Kan extension Lf_!: D(Fun(A,𝒜)) -> D(Fun(B,𝒜)) does exist for any Grothendieck abelian 𝒜 (e.g. sheaves of modules on a topos). One route: Ch(𝒜) carries a combinatorial injective model structure, so Fun(A,Ch(𝒜)) has a projective model structure and f_! ⊣ f^* is a Quillen pair. Exactness of the underived f_! is sufficient for the descent he describes, but not necessary.

At sheaf level, (f^o_top)_! always exists, since presheaf-topos morphisms induced by functors are essential. The real condition is only its exactness (e.g. f^o has cofiltered/filtered comma fibres, i.e. f^o_top is flat in the appropriate sense). The hedge 'si ... existe' is unnecessary.

Hyp 6 is false in general for the example just given, and for any non-trivial derivator. A 1-categorical localization need not be an ∞-categorical (Dwyer–Kan) localization. Example: let A be the poset of faces of the boundary of a 3-simplex, whose nerve is ≃ S^2, and invert all arrows. The 1-localization is equivalent to the point, but f^*: D(k) -> D(Fun(A,k-Mod)) is not fully faithful, since Ext^2(k,k) = H^2(S^2,k) ≠ 0. Hyp 6 holds only for 'homotopical' localizations, e.g. functors that are W-equivalences relative to a basic localizer in the sense of Ex 3, or when A is aspherical over B.

Minor: Hyp 5's gloss 'f^* f_! ≃ id, f^* f_* ≃ id' is correct for fully faithful f (pointwise Kan formulas). The parenthesis reads 'f_*, f_! pl. fid', and the formulas given are exactly that full faithfulness — consistent.

ideas.what: Derived category of A-diagrams with values in sheaves on a topos T, identified with sheaves on the product topos (A^o)^∧ × T. Restriction is the inverse image of a topos morphism; Rf_* is its derived right adjoint.
ideas.modern_name: Diagram derived categories / the represented derivator of an abelian (Grothendieck) category; sheaves on A^o×T
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA4 (Grothendieck–Verdier) for topos products; Grothendieck (Les Dérivateurs), Heller, Franke, Keller for the derivator viewpoint
ideas.where_published: SGA4 (topos products, essential morphisms); Les Dérivateurs (example of derivators from abelian/model categories)

ideas.what: Existence of Lf_! when the left Kan extension at sheaf level is exact.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; general existence via model structures (Hovey, Beke, Lurie) or Cisinski for derivators
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (axiom Der 3: existence of u_!, u_*)

ideas.what: Base change for cartesian squares: g^* f_! ≅ f'_! g'^* if f is an opfibration (or, questioned, g a fibration), and the dual for f_*.
ideas.modern_name: Proper/smooth base change in derivators: opfibrations are proper, fibrations are smooth
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Les Dérivateurs); Cisinski, 'Images directes cohomologiques dans les catégories de modèles' (2003); Maltsiniotis
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (smooth and proper functors, base change); related material in Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: Hyp 5: Kan extensions along fully faithful functors are fully faithful; f^* is a localization.
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness of u_!, u_* for fully faithful u (a consequence of Der 4)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck / Maltsiniotis (derivator theory); classical for ordinary Kan extensions

ideas.what: Hyp 6: restriction along a localization functor is fully faithful.
ideas.modern_name: Restriction along an ∞-localization is fully faithful (true for Dwyer–Kan/∞-localizations, false for mere 1-localizations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dwyer–Kan; Cisinski (Le localisateur fondamental minimal; Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to discussions of localizers/asphericity in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs; exact form unsure

missed.claim: G. asks with double question marks whether base change for f_! holds when, instead of f being cofibered, g is fibered (and dually). This is the proper vs smooth base-change dichotomy for derivators. It was later established (Cisinski 2003; Grothendieck, Les Dérivateurs), so it is not missed, but this page shows the dichotomy already formulated as a question in 1983.
missed.quote: g^* f_! ← f'_! g'^* si f cofibrant [ou g fibrant ??]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it dates the origin of the smooth/proper functor notions in derivator theory to the 1983 notes. No new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: These are early drafts of the derivator axioms (base change for fibrations/opfibrations, full faithfulness of Kan extensions), all later developed in Les Dérivateurs and by Cisinski and Maltsiniotis. Interesting are the early appearance of the smooth/proper question and an incorrect candidate axiom (Hyp 6) that would fail for derived categories, but nothing absent from the literature.

'indépendamment de g' before the base-change formulas is doubtful; the handwriting looks more like 'i.e. dans ce cas' or 'isomorphisme'. Uncertain.
The heading insertion likely reads 'Propriétés formelles impliquant les commutations [?] supérieures et produits [?]'. Highly uncertain.
'(par passage aux adjoints à droite, cf. ? g)' — the final token is probably a page reference ('p. 7?') or 'g'. Uncertain.
